subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
subcategory: Privacy Laws That Changed the World
title: Griswold v Connecticut
description: A short lesson to help you apply Griswold v Connecticut.

hook.text: In 1965, the Supreme Court struck down a law banning contraceptives — and discovered a right to privacy.

buildup.text: Connecticut had outlawed birth control. A doctor was fined for prescribing it to married couples.

discovery.text: The Court ruled that the Constitution implies a right to privacy, found in the 'penumbras' of several amendments.

twist.text: Privacy isn't explicitly mentioned in the Constitution. The Court had to read between the lines to find it.

climax.text: Griswold established that personal decisions about family life are protected from government intrusion.

punchline.text: Privacy found between the lines. A right implied.

quiz.question: What was significant about the Griswold v Connecticut ruling?
options: The Supreme Court recognized an implied constitutional right to privacy
It was the first case about internet privacy
It established the right to free speech online
